De Quervain syndrome

No animal evidence was identified in the exact or mapped clinical categories.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

No animal evidence was identified in the exact or mapped clinical categories.

Summary of the Evidence

The exact category contains two publications: a 2015 low-level laser versus ultrasound study and a 2023 sham-controlled high-intensity laser pilot. Citation search also identified a 2025 low-level laser comparison, a 2026 sham-controlled trial, and a 2025 meta-analysis. These reports do not show consistent superiority over standard care.

Human and clinical evidence

Sharma et al. compared low-level laser with ultrasound in 30 patients, but the small active-comparator study does not provide strong evidence of a specific PBM effect (2015). Chongkriengkrai et al. randomized 19 patients to high-intensity laser or sham, with both groups receiving a thumb-spica splint and exercise. Pain and disability improved from baseline in both groups, but there were no significant between-group differences (2023). A 72-person 2025 laser-versus-ultrasound trial reported a week-four pain difference favoring laser in its results, while its conclusion says laser was superior for disability but not pain, an internal inconsistency (Farooq et al. 2025). In 26 participants, a 2026 double-blind trial found that 1064-nm high-power laser plus splinting was not superior to sham plus splinting for pain or function (Sumanapun et al. 2026). A meta-analysis of three high-intensity trials found no significant pooled advantage for pain or disability (de la Barra Ortiz et al. 2025).

Animal evidence

No animal study was identified in the exact or mapped clinical evidence.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No standalone in-vitro or ex-vivo evidence was identified.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

Protocols include low-level laser, high-intensity laser, and 1064-nm high-power laser, with different comparators and co-interventions. The 2023 trial used nine sessions over three weeks with splinting and exercise in both arms. The 2026 study used 1064 nm at 8 W and nine sessions over three weeks, again with splinting in both groups. Different laser classes and doses should not be treated as a single intervention.

Interpretation

Current controlled evidence does not establish a reliable benefit beyond splinting, exercise, or ultrasound. The 2025 comparison is difficult to interpret because its abstract contradicts itself, and the pooled high-intensity estimate was not significant.

Evidence strength in source summaryVery low for pain and hand-function benefit beyond splinting or exercise
Publications and records2 publications.

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

Two exact-category trials and three later mapped reports provide mixed results. The 2023 sham-controlled pilot found no added benefit over splinting and exercise; the 2026 sham-controlled trial also found no superiority. A 2025 comparison reported contradictory pain conclusions, and a meta-analysis found no pooled advantage. Larger trials with consistent outcomes are needed.
